newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN WANTS FOURTH WIN AND A DRY RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN WANTS FOURTH WIN AND A DRY RACE.

text.p: Three times 500cc world champion Michael Doohan bids for his fourth win of the season at Sunday's Austrian Grand Prix and hopes the race will be spared a repeat of last year's rain.

Final qualifying was scrapped after torrential rain flooded the track and paddock in 1996 when the grand prix circus made its first visit to the revised A1-Ring, the track previously known as Zeltweg.
"The rain really affected things there last year when it dragged the dirt on to the track. I hope it will be a bit cleaner this year and in better condition," said Doohan.
The Australian was even indirectly struck by lightning during the storm when a small shock went down the stem of an umbrella he was holding.
In spite of the problems, Doohan led last season's Austrian race until a dramatic penultimate lap when he was overtaken by Spanish Honda team mate Alex Criville.
Doohan holds a 17-point championship lead over Criville, the only other winner this year.
Victory at the Italian Grand Prix two weeks ago allowed Doohan to equal late Briton Mike Hailwood's tally of 37 career 500cc wins. Only Italy's Giacomo Agostini scored more with 68.
Criville, second in Malaysia and Japan, will be trying to forget the Italian race where he had to use his spare Honda after his race bike failed in the warm-up lap.
Then a ninth lap error dropped Criville from second to 12th place, where he had to fight his way through the field to eventually finish fourth.
"I proved I could win against Doohan in Spain," Criville said. "The championship is far from over. Bad luck comes to some people but it will level out as the season goes on."
Other potential winners are Japanese Honda riders Nobuatsu Aoki and Tadayuki Okada, who have each made the podium twice, and Italian Luca Cadalora on a Yamaha.
Cadalora was the first non-Honda rider to make the season's rostrum when he was second in Italy.
